descriptionChirho: Denominative Piel verb from qen (nest), meaning to build a nest, to nest, to settle in a nest-like dwelling. Used literally of birds nesting in trees (Ps 104:17, Ezek 31:6 in figurative cedar imagery) and of the arrow-snake nesting in desolate ruins (Isa 34:15). Applied metaphorically to human habitation in an inaccessible high place like a bird's nest (Jer 48:28, of Moab nesting in cliff-sides; Jer 22:23 Ketiv/Qere of one nested in the cedars of Lebanon). Consistently rendered Arabic 'ashshasha (عَشَّشَ, to nest), Korean dungji teulda (둥지를 틀다, to build a nest), Hindi ghonsla banana (घोंसला बनाना, to make a nest), Spanish anidar (to nest), French nicher/faire un nid. All inflectional variants (Piel perfect, imperfect, Pual participle) express the same core sense.
